newsitem.title: JAPAN: TSE says to take strict action on Nomura scandal.
newsitem.headline: TSE says to take strict action on Nomura scandal.

text.p: The Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE) said on Friday that it would deal "in a strict manner" with the case of Nomura Securities Co Ltd, depending on the outcome of investigations into the scandal.

In a statement, TSE president Mitsuhide Yamaguchi said the arrest on Friday of a former Nomura president was a "very regrettable" development and that the bourse would act sternly over the affair, basing its actions on the results of prosecutors' investigations.
Nomura is a member of the TSE.

Former Nomura president Hideo Sakamaki was arrested on Friday on suspicion of conspiring with three Nomura executives to give 38.5 million yen to racketeer Ryuichi Koike, the figure at the centre of the widening loans and payoffs scandal, in March 1995.
Sakamaki stepped down in March when the scandal broke, becoming an adviser to the brokerage.
Prosecutors said they believed the money was given as an expression of appreciation for Koike's future cooperation in ensuring that a shareholders' meeting held a few months later went smoothly.
The Japan Securities Dealers Association (JSDA), of which Nomura Securities is also a member, issued a similar statement on Friday.
"We will deal with the Nomura case in a strict manner, based on the outcome of the investigations by legal authorities (expected to be unveiled) in the future," the JSDA said.
